Add the contrasts of a two-factor design to a sample annotation

Source: R/generatedContrastsDF.R
annotation_add_contrasts.Rd

Unites the two factor columns into a Group column and appends the contrasts of generate_contrasts() as the columns ContrastName and Contrast, in the layout of a prolfquapp dataset annotation. The shorter side is padded with NA rows: with fewer contrasts than samples the contrast columns, with more contrasts than samples the sample columns, so the extra rows carry only a contrast. Nothing is written to disk.

Usage

annotation_add_contrasts(
  df,
  primary_col,
  secondary_col,
  prefix = "G_",
  dataset_id = "dataset",
  decreasing = FALSE,
  interactions = TRUE
)

Arguments

df

data.frame with annotation data

primary_col

character, name of the primary factor column

secondary_col

character, name of the secondary factor column

prefix

character, prefix for output naming (default "G_")

dataset_id

character, dataset identifier for output naming

decreasing

logical, if TRUE sort factor levels in decreasing order

interactions

logical, if TRUE include interaction contrasts

Value

A list with annot, the annotation with the Group, ContrastName and Contrast columns (the two factor columns are dropped), and name, a suggested file name DEA_<prefix>_<dataset_id>.csv.

See also

Other contrasts: generate_contrasts(), generate_contrasts_for_factor(), interaction_contrasts(), level_specific_contrasts(), main_effect_contrasts()

Examples


# 2 genotypes x 3 time points x 6 replicates
design <- expand.grid(
  rep = 1:6, factor_B = c("T0", "T150", "T300"), factor_A = c("WT", "KO"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
annotation <- data.frame(
  Name = paste(design$factor_A, design$factor_B, design$rep, sep = "_"),
  factor_A = design$factor_A,
  factor_B = design$factor_B
)
annotation_add_contrasts(annotation, "factor_A", "factor_B", "primary")
